title: Special three-arrow hammocks compute hammock mapping spaces
statement:
A model category means a complete and cocomplete category $\mathcal M$ with classes $C,F,W$ of cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences. The class $W$ is retract closed and satisfies two-out-of-three, and $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system consists of factorizations of every map into its two classes, each class being exactly the maps with the diagonal-lifting property against the other. Trivial means also in $W$; an object is cofibrant if its initial map is in $C$, and fibrant if its terminal map is in $F$. Universes may be enlarged. Use the hammock construction $L^H(\mathcal M,W)$ of [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]. For $x,y\in\mathcal M$ define an ordinary category $\mathcal T(x,y)$. An object is a zigzag $x\xleftarrow{p}u\xrightarrow{f}v\xleftarrow{i}y$ with $p$ a trivial fibration and $i$ a trivial cofibration. A morphism from $(u,v,p,f,i)$ to $(u',v',p',f',i')$ is a pair $a:u\to u'$, $b:v\to v'$ satisfying $p'a=p$, $bi=i'$ and $bf=f'a$. Such $a,b$ are weak equivalences by two-out-of-three. Composition is componentwise composition. Reduction of strings of these commutative diagrams gives a simplicial map
$$N\mathcal T(x,y)\longrightarrow L^H(\mathcal M,W)(x,y).$$
This map is a weak homotopy equivalence. Pullback of $p$ along a map $x'\to x$ and pushout of $i$ along a map $y\to y'$ give the endpoint actions on $\mathcal T$; their comparisons with precomposition and postcomposition in $L^H$ commute up to the homotopies represented by the corresponding hammocks. An object with $p=i=1$ is sent to the length-one hammock of $f$. No cofibrancy, fibrancy, enrichment, properness or combinatoriality hypothesis is imposed on $x,y$ or $\mathcal M$.
